properties.title: Tornado Warning issued November 4 at 3:25PM CST until November 4 at 4:00PM CST by NWS Birmingham AL
properties.description:
TORBMX

The National Weather Service in Birmingham has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
East central Bibb County in central Alabama...

* Until 400 PM CST.

* At 325 PM CST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located near Ashby, or 10 miles east of Centreville, moving
northeast at 10 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed.
Damage to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree
damage is likely.

* Locations impacted include...
Brierfield Ironworks Park and Ashby.
properties.instruction:
TAKE COVER NOW! Move to a basement or an interior room on the lowest
floor of a sturdy building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors, in a
mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter
and protect yourself from flying debris.

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued November 4 at 4:10PM EST by NWS Peachtree City GA
properties.description:
At 410 PM EST, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Byron, or 11 miles south of Macon, moving northeast at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Up to 40 mph wind, frequent cloud to ground lightning and
heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect minor damage to tree limbs and blowing around of
light, unsecured objects. Heavy rain may cause temporary
street flooding especially in poor drainage areas.

Locations impacted include...
Macon, Warner Robins, Centerville, Byron, Robins AFB, Marion,
Middle Georgia Regional Airport, Rutland, Elberta, Skipperton,
Huber, Robins Air Force Base, Franklinton, Cross Keys, Jack Brown
Estates and Lakewood.
properties.instruction:
People outdoors should seek shelter immediately. If you can hear
thunder, you are close enough to be struck by lightning. Motorists
should slow down and be prepared for possible loss of control due to
hydroplaning.
